subject: Cross-border controls & DPA annex alignment — Omnicare RFP follow-up
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@omnicarehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Omnicare Legal Team <legal@omnicarehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: cross-border transfer controls for RFP OC-0487

Thanks Karthik — quick follow up after reviewing the DPA annex draft your team uploaded. We still need clarifications on two areas before sharing this with our data protection officer: 

1) Scope of international processing: your annex lists EU controller data pseudonymized, but Omnicare needs explicit mapping of which Redis/KV cache traffic will cross the Atlantic and under what routing policy.
2) Subprocessor chain: the RFP asked for subprocessor locations and whether any subprocessors persist token-level logs for longer than 7 days.

Can you provide a concise mapping (ideally a one-page table) and a statement of operational controls for KV cache replication and border routing? Also flag any sections that would require further legal review.

Attachment: Omnicare_RFP_Section_B_questions.xlsx (we've highlighted rows 5-9)

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our DPO wants an internal brief by next Tuesday.

—Samantha Reed
Head of Vendor Risk, Omnicare Health
Samantha.Reed@omnicarehealth.com
Phone: +1 415 555 0199

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@omnicarehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: cross-border transfer controls for RFP OC-0487

Samantha — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers up front, full annex map attached: 

- KV cache replication and routing: By default, KV cache instances are region-local (EU-only) for customers who opt for EU data residency. For Hosted customers without residency constraints, our smart routing may route read-only cache fetches to the nearest compatible region to reduce latency. For Omnicare we propose EU-only routing (no outbound cache reads to US). See attached annex map page 2 for the routing policy and kernel-level replication flags.

- Subprocessor persistence: Our subprocessors are listed in the annex with locations. We do not store token-level request payloads in any subprocessor beyond 7 days for production telemetry when EU residency is enforced; dev/test environments may retain logs longer but are excluded by contract. When you choose the Dedicated or Private deployment, customer-managed logging settings can further reduce retention.

Next steps I propose: 
- Please review the attached PDF (redwood-crossborder-annex-map-v1.pdf) — it has the one-page mapping you asked for.
- Ben can provide the technical appendix on KV cache networking if your infra team wants packet/port details.
- If the DPO needs legal language changes we can highlight redlines in the DPA annex.

Attachment: redwood-crossborder-annex-map-v1.pdf (annex map, routing table, subprocessor roster)

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Direct: +1 212 555 0142

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@omnicarehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: cross-border transfer controls for RFP OC-0487

Samantha — adding a couple operational details that often help the DPO triage: 

- Practical control: For the EU-only routing profile we enforce a hard policy at the load-balancer + orchestration layer; requests with non-EU source IPs that would otherwise trigger cross-region cache lookup are forced to a local fallback that does not query US-hosted caches.

- Audit evidence: We can provide a sample tracing span and a recent anonymized routing log extract (redacted) that shows region tag enforcement. That evidence is already used in several live customer audits.

- Retention & access: Role-based access controls prevent engineering-level read access to token-level telemetry; only the telemetry team (two named roles) has access and access is logged. We can bind this to an admin approval workflow for Omnicare.

I attached a small diagram of the KV-cache networking and a suggested line for the DPA annex legal team to accept (simple binding language we use with other EU health customers). If you'd like, Ben can join a short tech call with your infra folks early next week.

Attachments:
- kvcache-networking-diagram.png (diagram, 1 page)
- omnicare-multiparty-qna.xlsx (filled answers to rows 5-9)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Compliance Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@omnicarehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Omnicare Legal Team <legal@omnicarehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: cross-border transfer controls for RFP OC-0487

Thanks everyone — the annex map and the diagram look good and address the majority of questions. A couple of follow-ups from our legal and infra reviewers: 

- Legal would like the 7-day retention statement moved into a DPA annex clause (we can provide suggested wording).
- Infra would like the sample tracing span (anonymized) and confirmation there are no third-party CDN providers in the cache path for EU routing.

Can you: 
1) Draft the short DPA clause for retention and add it to the annex PDF (or provide it as plain text we can redline)?
2) Confirm and share the anonymized tracing span (redacted) and a short confirmation that no third-party CDN is used in the EU-only cache path.

If you can get those to me by end of Monday our DPO will sign off and we can move to contract redlines. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Samantha
Samantha Reed
Head of Vendor Risk, Omnicare Health
